job.title: HR Consultant
job.description:
We are partnering with a well-established and highly respected WA-based consulting business that has been supporting organisations across a diverse range of industries for more than 25 years.

Working directly with business owners, executives and operational leaders, you'll have the opportunity to deliver meaningful HR solutions that help businesses navigate complex people challenges and drive organisational success.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced HR professional who enjoys variety, autonomy, stakeholder engagement and partnering with clients to deliver practical, commercially focused outcomes.

The Opportunity
As an HR Consultant, you'll manage a portfolio of clients across a range of industries, providing strategic and operational HR support across the full employee lifecycle.

From employee relations matters and workplace investigations through to organisational change, leadership development, policy development and workforce planning, you'll play a key role in helping clients achieve their people and business objectives.

This is a genuine consulting role that offers exposure to diverse organisations, projects and challenges while building strong relationships with leaders and key stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide strategic and operational HR consulting services across a diverse client portfolio
  • Identify, develop and deliver tailored HR solutions aligned with client objectives
  • Advise on employee relations matters, performance management, disciplinary processes and workplace investigations
  • Provide guidance on Industrial Relations matters, including Awards, enterprise agreements and employment legislation
  • Develop and implement HR policies, procedures and frameworks aligned with best practice
  • Support workforce planning, talent management and recruitment initiatives
  • Conduct HR audits, reviews and organisational assessments
  • Facilitate training, leadership development and capability-building initiatives
  • Analyse workforce data and HR metrics to provide meaningful business insights
  • Support organisational change, restructures and transformation projects
  • Design and implement employee engagement and retention initiatives
  • Manage client relationships, project deliverables and consulting outcomes
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of consulting methodologies, tools and resources
  • Remain informed of legislative changes and emerging HR and Industrial Relations trends
About You 
  • A degree qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline
  • Minimum 4 years' experience in a HR generalist or HR consulting role
  • Strong knowledge of Australian employment legislation, Industrial Relations and HR compliance requirements
  • Experience managing employee relations matters and workplace investigations
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A proactive, solutions-focused and commercially minded approach
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and build strong client relationships
  • High levels of professionalism, accountability and initiative
  • Unrestricted working rights in Australia
What's on Offer?
  • Opportunity to work across a diverse portfolio of clients and industries
  • Exposure to complex and meaningful HR projects
  • Strong mentoring and support from experienced leaders
  • Career progression opportunities within a growing consultancy
  • Ongoing professional development and learning opportunities
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
  • Competitive salary package aligned to experience
If you're an experienced HR professional looking for a role that offers variety, professional growth and the opportunity to make a genuine impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or contact Hannah at a&co Recruitment Partners for a confidential discussion - hannah.lelliott@aandco.au

Working closely with People & Culture, Finance, Operations and key stakeholders across the business, you'll provide expert advice on complex payroll matters and play a key role in maintaining a high-performing payroll function.

  • Partner with leaders across HR, Finance and Operations to improve payroll processes and outcomes.
About You

You are an experienced payroll leader with a strong background in governance, compliance and operational leadership within a complex environment.

You'll bring:
  • Significant experience leading payroll teams and functions.
  • Strong knowledge of Australian payroll legislation, awards and enterprise agreements.
  • Experience managing payroll audits, compliance programs and risk frameworks.
  • Proven leadership capability with experience coaching and developing team members.
  • Exposure to payroll system implementations, upgrades or transformation projects.
  • SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll experience will be highly regarded. 
Why Talison Lithium?

This is an opportunity to join a respected industry leader and influence the ongoing evolution of payroll governance and service delivery. You'll work alongside a collaborative leadership team, lead an established function, and contribute to meaningful improvement initiatives that support a large and dynamic workforce.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Hannah Lelliott at A&Co Recruitment Partners, or apply today !

job.title: Financial Controller - 12 month Fixed-Term Contract
job.description:
Lead financial performance. Deliver commercial insight. Make an impact.
  
Piper Alderman is seeking an experienced and commercially minded Financial Controller to join the finance team on a 12 month fixed-term contract.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this is a key leadership role responsible for overseeing the firm's financial accounting, planning and reporting, budgeting, forecasting, taxation, treasury and accounts receivable functions.

Working closely with the CFO, Managing Partner, Partners and executive leadership team, you will provide trusted financial insight, strengthen financial governance and support informed commercial decision-making across the firm.
  
About the Role
As Financial Controller, you will take ownership of a broad range of financial management and operational responsibilities, including:
  • Financial planning and reporting: Oversee monthly financial statements, annual budgets, rolling forecasts, cash flow projections and management reporting packs.
  • Financial accounting and compliance: Manage month-end close, annual financial statements, accounting policies, taxation obligations, BAS and FBT reporting, and external audit processes.
  • Commercial and strategic support: Provide financial analysis and commercial advice to the CFO, Managing Partner, Finance Committee and executive leadership team.
  • Treasury and cash flow management: Manage liquidity, banking relationships, financing obligations, debt covenants and cash flow planning.
  • Accounts receivable and credit management: Lead the Accounts Receivable team, oversee WIP and debtor recoverability, and drive continuous improvement in credit management and collections.
  • Governance and risk: Champion the firm's Delegation of Authority framework, ensure compliance with financial policies and procedures, and oversee financial approvals and controls.
  • People leadership: Lead, support and develop the Finance and Accounts Receivable team, building technical capability, accountability and a culture of continuous improvement.
  • Systems and process improvement: Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, reporting, budgeting, forecasting and operational processes.
  
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • CA or CPA qualification and a Bachelor of Commerce, Accounting or equivalent relevant degree.
  • A minimum of 10 years' post-graduate experience in a senior finance or financial control role.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to work effectively with Partners, committees, executives and other stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management and financial analysis.
  • Proven people leadership skills, with the ability to motivate, develop and engage a finance team.
  • Strong knowledge of accounting standards, their practical application and Australian taxation requirements.
  • Advanced Excel skills and confidence working with financial systems, reporting tools and budgeting and forecasting platforms.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgement and maintain confidentiality when dealing with sensitive financial information.
  • Experience within a professional services or partnership environment would be advantageous.
  
Why Join Piper Alderman?
Piper Alderman offers the opportunity to work in a respected professional services firm in a role with broad financial responsibility and meaningful engagement with senior leadership.
You will have the opportunity to:
  • Partner closely with the CFO and senior leadership team on financial and commercial matters.
  • Influence financial performance, reporting quality and business decision-making.
  • Lead and develop a team while contributing to continuous improvement across finance operations.
  • Apply your expertise across a diverse range of financial management, governance and operational responsibilities.
  
This is an excellent opportunity for a senior finance professional who thrives in a complex professional services environment, combines strong technical expertise with commercial acumen, and enjoys leading and developing a high-performing team.
  
Like to know more?
If you’re interested in this opportunity, apply now with a short a cover letter and resume. For a confidential discussion, contact Phil Scardigno at a&co Recruitment Partners on 0439 074 202 or email phil.scardigno@aandco.au
  
All applications will be treated in strict confidence.
